Forum Triage

Find discussions that need attention without ranking students, while preserving Moodle forum visibility, group and capability rules end to end.

Supported scope
Visible course forum discussions
Design focus
Teacher attention, not learner scoring
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Deterministic priority
Calculate unanswered age, teacher reply state, long-thread thresholds and objective priority in PHP.
✓
Forum rules preserved
Use Moodle's forum APIs and visibility checks rather than bypassing separate groups or private reply rules.
✓
AI for semantics only
Detect possibly unresolved discussions, summarize topics and cluster recurring questions without overriding priority.
Pseudonymized prompts
Replace authors with request-local identifiers such as U1 and T1.
Bounded discussion text
Send only the first post and a limited number of recent visible replies, converted to plain text and truncated.
No persistence
Do not store prompts, raw AI responses or triage analyses.
What this plugin does

Forum Triage addresses the teacher's practical question: where should I look first? Moodle determines what the teacher can see and the plugin computes factual thread state before any semantic model call.

AI may help describe whether a thread still sounds unresolved or group recurring questions, but it cannot raise or lower the authoritative priority calculated from visible forum facts.

Features you get
Needs-attention view
Surface high- and medium-priority discussion states.
No-response filter
Find discussions with no visible reply.
Possibly unresolved
Add semantic review without treating it as a fact.
Recurring questions
Cluster similar visible questions for teacher follow-up.
Forum/group filters
Filter by forum, visible group, activity period and teacher-reply state.
Direct discussion links
Open the exact Moodle discussion from each result.

Also requires AI Bridge.
